verdict.rationale: Twenty documents a developer-first public API with both REST and GraphQL endpoints. Every object, including custom ones, gets its own endpoints, and a Metadata API handles schema changes. The API also supports batching, role-scoped API keys and an interactive playground, and a community user reports the REST API "worked ok." missing for 10: a static public OpenAPI spec (the probe found 404s at standard paths; docs are instead auto-generated per workspace), and deeper independent hands-on corroboration of API reliability.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Both GraphQL and REST endpoints, with auto-generated documentation per workspace.
Schema management: create/modify/delete objects, fields, and relations. This is how you programmatically change your data model.
Both REST and GraphQL support batching up to 60 records per request — create, update, or delete.
It includes an interactive playground where you can execute real calls against your data.
